newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate falls to 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate falls to 5.5 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.5 percent on Monday due to aggressive lending by foreign banks as well as easy availability of funds in the overnight market, dealers said.
The rate was at 5.8 percent on Friday.
Dealers said there was no sign of Bank Negara's support at 5.8 percent, which has been widely accepted as the central bank's floor rate.
"Foreign banks are holding a lot of money and lending heavily in the overnight market," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "But it looks like the overnight is bottoming out at 5.5 percent."
Dealers said the market remained flush, with some of the liquidity said to be provided by Bank Negara.
But there could be some fund tightness on Wednesday due to payment for Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit against a maturity of 500 million, they said.
Earlier, interbank rates rose across the board on demand from finance companies and lingering fears of a long-term government bond issue.
One-week money was up at 6.70/80 percent against 6.50 on Friday, but two-week was unchanged at 6.70/80 percent.
One-month money was at 7.40 percent against 7.30/35, three-month at 7.50/55 against 7.40/45 and six-month at 7.55/60 against 7.45/50.
"Finance companies are short again. They are pushing up rates," said one dealer.
"But, the big banks are up there lending. One of the big banks has set the cap on one-month at 7.40," he said.
Dealers said rumours of a new bond issue was preventing any fall in rates.

Rumours of a new bond issue first surfaced a few months ago following maturity of a series of bond issues which were not rolled over. Bank Negara last issued long-term government bonds in November 1996.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point to 92.63, or an implied yield of 7.37 percent.
The December contract also fell one to 92.74, or 7.26 percent while March 1998 was down two to 92.76, or 7.24 percent.
